summary: Created one evidence-linked nuclear and uranium fuel-cycle idea. Current IEA evidence supports concentrated mining, conversion, and enrichment capacity, while Cameco contracting demonstrates long-duration demand. Supply response, operational execution, contract lag, and valuation block a strategy; no ticker-only follow-up was created.

evidence.source: International Energy Agency, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026
evidence.claim: The IEA identifies conversion as the most immediate nuclear-fuel bottleneck and reports that the top three countries account for nearly three-quarters of uranium mining and about 70% of conversion and enrichment capacity.

evidence.source: International Energy Agency, Global Energy Review 2026
evidence.claim: The IEA reports 78 GW of nuclear capacity under construction across 15 countries and ten construction starts totaling 12.2 GW in 2025.
Cameco agreed to supply India nearly 22 million pounds over 2027-2035 on market-related terms with an estimated CAD 2.6 billion contract value.
Cameco disclosed average annual committed uranium deliveries above 28 million pounds for 2026-2030 and unchanged operating guidance, while emphasizing quarterly delivery variability.

daily_report_items: Researched nuclear and uranium fuel-cycle bottlenecks: concentration and long-term demand are supported, but contract conversion, operating reliability, supply response, and valuation block a strategy.
